source_row.rationale: Long-standing gastroesophageal reflux is the usual precipitating factor for acquired Barrett esophagus, making Option B correct. Achalasia is an esophageal motility disorder, esophageal varices are primarily related to portal hypertension, and Zenker diverticulum is a pharyngoesophageal pouch rather than the characteristic metaplastic complication of chronic GERD.
source_row.source_detail: StatPearls Barrett Esophagus — Introduction/Etiology: Barrett esophagus is intestinal metaplasia of the distal esophagus; most cases are acquired and the usual precipitant is long-standing gastroesophageal reflux disease, with increased esophageal adenocarcinoma risk. StatPearls Barrett Esophagus updated 2025-05-26 and current in StatPearls [Internet] 2026; NCBI source live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, endocrine/vascular emergencies and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
